transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.

input.query: SELECT 'n' p, service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'a', service_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Search latency jumped (client about 1.8 ms to 55 ms, server about 3.7 ms to 110 ms), and span counts shifted for several services. Next I'll break the spans down by name, pod and status.

input.query: SELECT 'n' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, max(duration)/1e6 max_ms, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods, group_concat(DISTINCT attr_http_response_status_code) codes FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'a', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, max(duration)/1e6, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name), group_concat(DISTINCT attr_http_response_status_code) FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,4,1

input.query: SELECT 'n' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('search','frontend','reservation','profile','rate') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'a', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('search','frontend','reservation','profile','rate') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,4,1

content.text: The key pattern is `search → rate.GetRates`: about 110 ms per call versus 3 ms normally, and only one `rate` server span appears in the incident window. Next I'll check restarts, uptime and per-connection network metrics.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avg_v, round(max(value),2) max_v FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'NORMAL:'||metric, service_name, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*), round(avg(value),2), round(max(value),2) FROM normal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 1,2

input.query: SELECT metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs, count(DISTINCT attr_source) srcs, round(avg(value),2) avg_v, round(max(value),2) max_v FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs, count(DISTINCT attr_source) srcs, round(avg(value),2) avg_v, round(max(value),2) max_v FROM normal_metrics_sum GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: No per-connection network metrics are present. Next I'll look at the container and JVM metrics, restarts and uptime, per service, in both periods.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),3) avg_v, round(max(value),3) max_v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime','container.cpu.utilization','container.memory.usage') OR metric LIKE '%cpu%' OR metric LIKE '%memory%' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: That output was too broad. I'll narrow to restarts and uptime, which are the signals that separate pod faults from saturation.

input.query: SELECT 'a' p, metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*) n, round(min(value),1) min_v, round(max(value),1) max_v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'n', metric, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*), round(min(value),1), round(max(value),1) FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 3,2,1

content.text: No restarts occurred in the incident window (user's count is constant at 7 in both periods), so this is not a pod restart. Next I'll check whether the slow `search → rate` calls have matching server spans in `rate`, and whether `abnormal_logs` is really empty.

input.query: SELECT c.attr_k8s_pod_name client_pod, c.attr_k8s_namespace_name ns, count(*) n, round(avg(c.duration)/1e6,1) avg_client_ms, round(min(c.duration)/1e6,1) min_ms, round(max(c.duration)/1e6,1) max_ms, count(s.span_id) matched_server, round(avg(s.duration)/1e6,2) avg_server_ms, group_concat(DISTINCT s.attr_k8s_pod_name) server_pods FROM abnormal_traces c LEFT JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.trace_id=c.trace_id AND s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND c.attr_span_kind='Client' GROUP BY 1,2
SELECT service_name, level, count(*) n FROM normal_logs GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: The client spans have no pod names, and the slow `search → rate.Rate/GetRates` calls run up to about 20 s with almost no matching server spans. I'll look at the duration distribution and the trace shape to understand what happens to these requests.

input.query: SELECT 'a' p, CASE WHEN duration<1e6 THEN '<1ms' WHEN duration<10e6 THEN '1-10ms' WHEN duration<100e6 THEN '10-100ms' WHEN duration<1000e6 THEN '0.1-1s' WHEN duration<10000e6 THEN '1-10s' ELSE '>=10s' END bucket, count(*) n FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND attr_span_kind='Client' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'n', CASE WHEN duration<1e6 THEN '<1ms' WHEN duration<10e6 THEN '1-10ms' WHEN duration<100e6 THEN '10-100ms' WHEN duration<1000e6 THEN '0.1-1s' WHEN duration<10000e6 THEN '1-10s' ELSE '>=10s' END, count(*) FROM normal_traces WHERE span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND attr_span_kind='Client' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT s.service_name svc, s.span_name, s.attr_span_kind kind, count(*) n, round(avg(s.duration)/1e6,1) avg_ms, round(min(s.duration)/1e6,1) min_ms, round(max(s.duration)/1e6,1) max_ms, sum(CASE WHEN s.attr_status_code<>'Unset' AND s.attr_status_code<>'OK' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) nonok FROM abnormal_traces s WHERE s.trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' AND attr_span_kind='Client' AND duration>1e9) GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2,3

content.text: The average was misleading: 360 of the 364 `rate` calls are under 1 ms, and only two are about 20 s. I'll check the time windows and what a typical abnormal request trace contains.

input.query: SELECT 'a' p, min(time) t0, max(time) t1, count(DISTINCT trace_id) traces, count(*) spans FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'n', min(time), max(time), count(DISTINCT trace_id), count(*) FROM normal_traces

SELECT trace_id, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, attr_k8s_pod_name, round(duration/1e6,2) ms, attr_status_code, attr_http_response_status_code FROM abnormal_traces WHERE trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='search' AND attr_span_kind='Server' LIMIT 3) ORDER BY trace_id, time
